lessons.title: The packing line and start-up
lessons.html:
Sections of a packing line

A fruit packing line is a set of connected machines that move fruit from the bin to the packed carton. The operator is responsible for running the line safely, keeping fruit flowing evenly and protecting fruit quality.

SectionFunction
Bin tipper / water dumpEmpties bins gently, often into water to cushion the fruit
Elevators and conveyorsMove fruit between sections
Pre-sort tableRemoves rotten fruit and foreign material
Washer and brushesClean the fruit
Treatment applicatorsApply approved treatments according to the programme
Drying tunnelDries fruit after washing or before and after waxing
WaxerApplies coating where required
Grading tablesGraders separate fruit into classes
SizerSeparates by size or weight into lanes
Packing stations, check-weighers, labellersPack, weigh and mark cartons

Pre-start checks

  1. Get the daily run plan: producers, cultivars, markets, programmes and expected volumes.
  2. Check the line was cleaned and sanitised; no tools or objects left on it.
  3. Check all guards, covers and interlocks are in place, and test emergency stops and pull-cords.
  4. Check water levels and quality in dump tanks, treatment tank levels, and that heaters and dryers reach set temperatures.
  5. Inspect belts, rollers, brushes and chains for wear, tracking and tension.
  6. Check compressed air, electrical panels (closed and dry) and lubrication.
  7. Sound the start-up warning and make sure everyone is clear of moving parts before starting.
  8. Start sections in the correct sequence, usually from the end of the line backwards, so fruit does not pile up.

Record the checks. If any safety device fails, do not start; report it and follow lockout procedure.

lessons.title: Running, troubleshooting and shutdown
lessons.html:
Controlling flow

The line works best with an even, steady flow. Too much fruit causes pile-ups, bruising, poor grading and mis-sizing. Too little wastes labour and capacity.

  • Set the tipper rate and conveyor speeds to match the capacity of graders, the sizer and packers.
  • Watch for build-ups at transfer points and drops. Fruit should roll, not fall.
  • Communicate with graders, sizer operator and packing supervisor about changes in volume, quality or market.

Batch changes

When changing producer, cultivar or market, run the line empty or use a clear gap so batches do not mix. Change treatments, labels and programmes as the plan requires. Record the time of each change for traceability.

Monitoring

  • Fruit damage: check for bruises, cuts or punctures caused by the line. Find and fix sharp edges, worn brushes or high drops.
  • Water and treatment levels and temperatures, dryer temperatures, and wax coverage.
  • Machine condition: noise, vibration, overheating motors, slipping or mistracking belts.

Troubleshooting

ProblemLikely causeAction
Fruit wet after dryerDryer too cool, airflow blocked, line too fastCheck settings and filters; adjust speed
Pile-up at a sectionDownstream stoppage or speed mismatchReduce infeed; find the cause downstream
Belt mistrackingTension or alignment faultStop, lock out and adjust or call maintenance
Increase in fruit damageWorn part, sharp edge, high dropLocate and correct, inform supervisor

Lockout and safety

Never reach into a running machine. Before clearing jams, adjusting or cleaning, stop the line, isolate the energy source, fit your personal lock and tag, and test that it cannot start. Only you remove your lock. Wear hearing protection, keep loose clothing and hair secured, and keep walkways clear.

Shutdown

  1. Stop the infeed and run all fruit off the line.
  2. Stop sections in the correct sequence.
  3. Drain and clean tanks per procedure, disposing of solutions through approved systems.
  4. Clean and sanitise according to the cleaning schedule.
  5. Report faults and wear for maintenance, and complete the shift log: volumes run, batch change times, downtime and causes.

Key points

  • Know each section of the line and its function.
  • Complete and record pre-start safety and condition checks.
  • Keep flow even and separate batches clearly at changeovers.
  • Monitor fruit damage, treatment and dryer settings, and machine condition.
  • Always lock out before clearing jams or cleaning; record the shift log.

quiz.question: Why are bins often tipped into water?

options.text: To cushion the fruit and reduce bruising

quiz.question: In which order are line sections usually started?

options.text: From the end of the line backwards
All at once with the infeed running

quiz.question: What should be done at a batch change?

options.text: Run the line empty or leave a clear gap and record the time

quiz.question: Fruit is still wet after the drying tunnel. What is a likely cause?

options.text: Dryer too cool, airflow blocked or line too fast
